title: Prior Authorization Metrics Provide New Insights into Insurer Practices, but Gaps Remain
key_claim: In the first year of federally mandated public reporting, standard prior authorization denial rates were 12% in Medicare Advantage, 14% in Medicaid managed care and 18% in the ACA federally facilitated Marketplace, with 67%, 47% and 43% of appealed denials overturned respectively.
frame_summary: Argues the new disclosures are a real but incomplete accountability instrument, and that the fix is better reporting standards rather than a change in how denial economics work.
verbatim_quote: Medicare Advantage insurers denied 12% of standard prior authorization requests, Medicaid managed care insurers denied 14%, and ACA Marketplace insurers denied 18%.
verbatim_list: Sixty-seven percent of prior authorization denials were overturned upon appeal in Medicare Advantage, 47% were overturned upon appeal in Medicaid managed care, and 43% were overturned in the ACA federally facilitated Marketplace.
For example, UnitedHealth denied 17% of standard requests in Medicare Advantage, 11% in Medicaid managed care, and 21% in the ACA Marketplace.

title: CMS-0057-F: Using Public Payor Prior Authorization Data
date_evidence:
CMS-0057-F: Using Public Payor Prior Authorization Data

August 18, 2026
key_claim: Across the aggregated first-year disclosures, 52.6% of appealed denials were overturned at the median plan while only 7.3% of denials were appealed, and 92% of the plans required to publish had done so by 21 July 2026.
frame_summary: Argues providers should treat the new disclosures as a commercial input for revenue cycle and payer negotiation, which reads the data as leverage rather than as evidence about how denial economics work.
verbatim_quote: More than half (52.6%) of appealed denials were overturned at the median plan, yet only 7.3% of denials were appealed.
verbatim_list: According to the AuthDenied database, as of July 21, 2026, 92% of payor plans required to publish CY 2025 performance metrics publicly have done so.
On March 31, 2026, one of the most significant components of

took effect: impacted payors were required to publicly report prior authorization metrics covering calendar year (CY) 2025. Required metrics include authorization volumes, approval and denial rates, appeal outcomes, and average decision turnaround times.

title: WISeR (Wasteful and Inappropriate Service Reduction) Model
key_claim: CMS pays WISeR model participants a percentage of the expenditures associated with care their reviews avert, across six performance years from January 2026 to December 2031 in six states.
frame_summary: Argues the model is a taxpayer-protection instrument that leaves coverage and payment policy untouched, presenting contingency payment to review vendors as a performance mechanism rather than as a change in who decides coverage.
verbatim_quote: Model participants receive a percentage of the expenditures associated with averted wasteful, inappropriate care as a result of their reviews. That percentage is adjusted based on the participant’s performance on measures related to the process, including provider experience.
verbatim_list: WISeR will run for six performance years from January 1, 2026 to December 31, 2031 in six states: New Jersey, Ohio, Oklahoma, Texas, Arizona, and Washington.

WISeR is the first Innovation Center model in which technology innovators are the only model participants, and it is also the first model that incentivizes the use of cutting-edge tools to ensure that payment complies with Medicare documentation, coverage, payment and coding rules.
All recommendations for non-payment are determined by appropriately licensed clinicians who will apply standardized, transparent and evidence-based procedures to their review.

title: Automation in Medicaid Prior Authorization: Recommendations
key_claim: MACPAC has recommended to Congress that CMS clarify the role of human oversight in Medicaid prior authorization and require disclosure of managed care plans' use of automation.
frame_summary: Argues that automated prior authorization needs human accountability and disclosure rules written before the tools scale, framing the problem as one of oversight design rather than of the incentives facing whoever runs the review.
verbatim_quote: The recommendations seek to clarify the role of human oversight in PA and increase transparency into managed care plans’ use of automation in the Medicaid PA process.
verbatim_list: The Commission conducted a study to understand the extent to which states, managed care plans, and providers use automation (i.e., artificial intelligence and algorithms) in the Medicaid PA process and to identify potential policy levers to oversee its use.
notes: Commission session presenting the four policy recommendations that became Chapter 2 of the June 2026 Report to Congress. Quote provenance: host not fetchable from the sandbox; quote read by hand off the live page during the 23/08/2026 WebFetch sweep.

title: Examining the Potential Impact of Medicare's New WISeR Model
key_claim: Services covered by the WISeR model accounted for 5.3% ($12.3B) of Part B spending in traditional Medicare in 2024, and the model's payment design rewards vendors partly on the volume of care they deny.
frame_summary: Argues the model's first-year spending effect will be modest and that the live risk sits in its payment incentives and in any future expansion, rather than in the technology itself.
verbatim_quote: about the financial incentives inherent in the WISeR model, which rewards vendors, in large part, based on the volume of care that they deny, creating financial incentives to maximize denials.
verbatim_list: WISeR services accounted for 5.3% ($12.3B) of all Part B spending in traditional Medicare in 2024, up from 1.1% ($2.4B) in 2019.
Prior authorization requirements are rare in traditional Medicare.

title: Prior authorization denials vary widely among insurers, first-of-its-kind data shows
key_claim: Trade coverage of the first public denial disclosures notes that high denial rates coexist with high appeal-overturn rates because very few people appeal.
frame_summary: Frames the disclosures as a first look behind the curtain on insurer behaviour, reading the story as one of variation between insurers rather than of the appeal rate that makes denial durable.
verbatim_quote: High denial rates are concerning given many denied items and services are approved upon appeal — but very few people actually appeal initial denials, according to past research.
verbatim_list: It’s the first peek behind the curtain at insurers’ prior authorization denial metrics, after the federal government began requiring insurers to post publicly available data this year.

Insurers are only required to report percentages, not the total number of prior authorization requests for each metric, making it difficult to fully understand the actual volume of denials, for example.

title: Senate Republicans kill bid to end Medicare prior authorization pilot
key_claim: A Congressional Review Act attempt to end the WISeR model failed on a party-line Senate vote on 16 July 2026, leaving the model running to its scheduled end in 2031.
frame_summary: Frames the vote as a partisan fight about whether AI review delays seniors' care, treating the contest as being about the technology rather than about the contingency payment behind it.
verbatim_quote: Senate Democrats’ bid to end a pilot program that adds artificial intelligence-backed prior authorization for some services in Medicare failed on Thursday.
verbatim_list: WISeR is a departure from the norm in Medicare, which largely doesn’t require pre-approvals for services.

Under the pilot, the federal government contracts with private companies to add prior authorizations for certain services deemed vulnerable to abuse and wasteful spending, like skin and tissue substitutes or epidural steroid injections for pain management.
